name: Vasa Museum
description: A museum built around the Vasa, a 17th-century warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was raised almost intact in 1961.

name: Stortorget
description: The old town’s main square, ringed by tall merchants’ houses in red and ochre. In 1520 it was the scene of the Stockholm Bloodbath.

name: Sergels torg
description: The city’s central sunken plaza, with black-and-white triangle paving and a glass obelisk, next to the Kulturhuset arts centre.

name: Olof Palme murder site
description: The spot on Sveavägen where Prime Minister Olof Palme was shot dead in 1986, marked by a plaque in the pavement.

name: Norrmalmstorg
description: A city-centre square where a 1973 bank robbery and hostage siege gave the world the term “Stockholm syndrome”.

name: Drottningholm Palace
description: The Swedish royal family’s home, on an island west of the city, with baroque gardens and an 18th-century court theatre still in working order.

name: Kungsträdgården
description: A central park and public square, once the royal kitchen garden, used for outdoor events. Its cherry trees blossom in spring.

name: Parliament House
description: The home of Sweden’s parliament, the Riksdag, on a small island between the old town and the city centre.

name: Raoul Wallenbergs torg
description: A waterside square named after the Swedish diplomat who saved thousands of Hungarian Jews in 1944, with a memorial to him.

name: ABBA The Museum
description: A museum on Djurgården about the Swedish pop group, with stage costumes, gold records and rooms where you can sing along.
